answer: Admit newcomers only through a narrow inlet: each funding cluster gets one inlet slot per epoch, so N shells queue N epochs. To claim a slot, an identity must forge its entry token in a public sequential forge: address-seeded work that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be split across machines, so N tokens cost N full forge runs. A rotating nebula of random peers then rechecks each token; the nebula cannot be predicted, so clones cannot pre-arrange cover. If two tokens trace to one funder, the nebula merges them into one standing and burns every linked bond multiplied by the merged count.
